question: When a bridge-backed Vercel AI SDK harness is configured with deterministic mintBridgeToken(sandboxId), can callers persist the returned detach or suspend lifecycle state without persisting the live bridge authentication token?

sources.name: Vercel AI SDK mintBridgeToken merge commit
sources.claim: The feature was introduced so callers able to derive a bridge token from sandbox id could reconstruct resume state without storing the secret; merged tests intentionally persist the token for live attach and expect the mint function not to run again on attach.

sources.name: Claude Code harness lifecycle implementation
sources.claim: Live bridge coordinates require token; detach and suspend serialize bridgeToken; successful attach consumes coords.token; mintBridgeToken runs on spawn or respawn.

sources.name: Workflow harness state and resume persistence documentation
sources.claim: Workflow consumers are instructed to persist the opaque resumeFrom state by session id; the documented example writes JSON.stringify(resumeState) to storage.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: Returned live resume state contains the caller-minted token and attach succeeds without another mint call.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The current public lifecycle contract still requires persistence of the live bridge credential for attach.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: A token-scrubbed bridge coordinate state is rejected by the current coordinate contract.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Callers cannot simply remove the credential and rely on mintBridgeToken to reconstruct it through the supported state shape.

stop_condition: Stop once the pinned source, merged tests, official workflow persistence path, and one executable discriminator agree on whether secretless live resume exists.
